```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

**Status: EXPLORATORY and non-causal.** The question is whether wheat roots are less colonized in
pots where fava grew more (an antagonistic fava-AMF relationship). Fava biomass is not randomized, and
the arrow could just as well run the other way: the Figure 3 analysis (`14_Figure3_FavaSuppression`) found that
inoculated wheat *suppresses* fava. So a negative slope here would show that the two move together, not
that fava reduces colonization. Every p-value is unadjusted for multiplicity.

**Data.** Parts 1-2 use intercrop pots only (n = 30, 5 per Inoc x Water cell), per pot. Part 3 uses both stand types. X-axis is `Fava_g`.
Colonization was scored on 100 root intersects per pot, so the three AMF metrics are counts out of 100:

* **Any fungal structure** (`hyph_n`, the hyphal colonization used elsewhere).
* **Arbuscules** (`arb_n`).
* **Vesicles** (`ves_n`).

`AV` (log arbuscule : vesicle ratio) is reported in the table only. It is set to 0 whenever both counts
are 0, so it is not defined for most sterile pots and is not plotted.

**Models.** Quasibinomial regression on the counts out of 100 (logit link, dispersion estimated, because
intersects within a root are not independent). Slopes are on the logit scale. `lm` for `AV`. Slopes come
from models fitted once with `emtrends`; no subset models.

```{r libs}
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
source("../fig_style.R")

inter <- readRDS("../wheat_audited.rds") %>% filter(Poly == "Inter")
stopifnot(nrow(inter) == 30, all(table(inter$Inoc, inter$Water) == 5),
          identical(levels(inter$Inoc), c("Inoc", "Strl")),
          all(inter$hyph_n == 100 - inter$None))

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3)))

metric_lab <- c(hyph_n = "Any fungal structure", arb_n = "Arbuscules", ves_n = "Vesicles")

fit_metric <- function(metric, rhs, data = inter) {
  if (metric == "AV") return(lm(as.formula(paste("AV ~", rhs)), data = data))
  data$n <- data[[metric]]
  glm(as.formula(paste("cbind(n, 100 - n) ~", rhs)), family = quasibinomial, data = data)
}
slopes <- function(m, by = NULL) {
  f <- if (is.null(by)) ~ 1 else as.formula(paste("~", by))
  as.data.frame(test(emtrends(m, f, var = "Fava_g")))
}
norm_cl <- function(d) {
  names(d)[names(d) == "prob"] <- "response"
  names(d)[names(d) %in% c("lower.CL", "asymp.LCL")] <- "lcl"
  names(d)[names(d) %in% c("upper.CL", "asymp.UCL")] <- "ucl"
  d
}
blue <- pal_poly[["Inter"]]
```

# Why two views

Fava biomass is nearly a proxy for inoculation (sterile pots grew 4-10 g of fava; inoculated pots 1-4 g),
and sterile pots are barely colonized (the scored colonization there is background/contamination). A
pooled regression over all 30 pots therefore mostly re-draws the inoculation effect. The informative
question is whether fava predicts colonization *among the inoculated pots*, where colonization actually
varies, so Part 2 estimates the slope within each inoculation treatment.

```{r summ}
inter %>% group_by(Inoc) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), `fava, g (range)` = paste0(round(min(Fava_g), 1), "-", round(max(Fava_g), 1)),
            `any structure, mean` = mean(hyph_n) / 100, `arbuscules, mean` = mean(arb_n) / 100,
            `vesicles, mean` = mean(ves_n) / 100) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>% knitr::kable()
```

# Part 1 - Simple regression, all 30 intercrop pots

* **pooled** p: `metric ~ Fava` (the simple regression).
* **adjusted** p: `metric ~ Fava + Inoc`, the fava slope once inoculation is accounted for.

```{r modelsA}
metrics <- c("hyph_n", "arb_n", "ves_n", "AV")
mA <- map(set_names(metrics), ~ list(pooled = fit_metric(.x, "Fava_g"),
                                      adj    = fit_metric(.x, "Fava_g + Inoc")))
slopeA <- imap_dfr(mA, ~ bind_rows(slopes(.x$pooled) %>% mutate(kind = "pooled"),
                                   slopes(.x$adj)    %>% mutate(kind = "adjusted")) %>%
                     mutate(metric = .y))
slopeA %>% transmute(metric, kind, slope = round(Fava_g.trend, 3), SE = round(SE, 3),
                     p = signif(p.value, 3)) %>% knitr::kable()
```

```{r figA, fig.width=10.5, fig.height=4.6}
grid <- seq(1, 10, length.out = 100)
plot_metrics <- c("hyph_n", "arb_n", "ves_n")
rel <- function(d) mutate(d, metric = factor(metric, plot_metrics, metric_lab))

linesA <- map_dfr(plot_metrics, ~ emmeans(mA[[.x]]$pooled, ~ Fava_g, at = list(Fava_g = grid),
                                          type = "response") %>% as.data.frame() %>% norm_cl() %>%
                    mutate(metric = .x)) %>% rel()
ptsA <- inter %>% select(Inoc, Water, Fava_g, all_of(plot_metrics)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(plot_metrics), names_to = "metric", values_to = "n") %>%
  mutate(y = n / 100) %>% rel()
annA <- slopeA %>% filter(metric %in% plot_metrics) %>% select(metric, kind, p.value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = kind, values_from = p.value) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("slope ", fmt_p(pooled), " (pooled)\nslope ", fmt_p(adjusted), " (adj. for Inoc)")) %>% rel()

figA <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = linesA, aes(Fava_g, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), fill = blue, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = linesA, aes(Fava_g, response), color = blue, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = ptsA, aes(Fava_g, y, fill = Inoc), shape = 21, color = blue, size = 3, stroke = 1) +
  geom_text(data = annA, aes(x = Inf, y = 1.3, label = label), hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1,
            size = 3, color = "grey25", lineheight = 0.95) +
  facet_wrap(~metric) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Inoc = blue, Strl = "white"), labels = inoc_lab) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.3), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Fava biomass (g per pot)", y = "% of root intersects",
       title = "AMF colonization against fava biomass, inter only",
       subtitle = "Line = pooled fit with 95% CI.") +
  theme_ms(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey93", linewidth = 0.3),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey30"))
figA
ggsave("figures/Fig_AMFvsFava_AllPots.pdf", figA, width = 10.5, height = 4.6)
ggsave("figures/Fig_AMFvsFava_AllPots.png", figA, width = 10.5, height = 4.6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

# Part 2 - Within each inoculation treatment (n = 15 each)

* **pooled** p: `metric ~ Fava * Inoc`, the simple fava slope within each treatment.
* **adjusted** p: `metric ~ Fava * Inoc + Water`, the same slope after accounting for water.

The sterile row is shown for completeness, but its "colonization" is contamination; the inoculated row
is the real test of antagonism. Within inoculated pots fava varies only about 1.3-4.3 g, and
colonization is near the ceiling for hyphae (0.46-1.0), so power is limited.

```{r modelsB}
mB <- map(set_names(metrics), ~ list(pooled = fit_metric(.x, "Fava_g * Inoc"),
                                      adj    = fit_metric(.x, "Fava_g * Inoc + Water")))
slopeB <- imap_dfr(mB, ~ bind_rows(slopes(.x$pooled, "Inoc") %>% mutate(kind = "pooled"),
                                   slopes(.x$adj,    "Inoc") %>% mutate(kind = "adjusted")) %>%
                     mutate(metric = .y))
slopeB %>% transmute(metric, Inoc, kind, slope = round(Fava_g.trend, 3), SE = round(SE, 3),
                     p = signif(p.value, 3)) %>% arrange(metric, Inoc, kind) %>% knitr::kable()
```

```{r figB, fig.width=10.5, fig.height=7}
rngB <- inter %>% group_by(Inoc) %>% summarise(lo = min(Fava_g), hi = max(Fava_g))
linesB <- map_dfr(plot_metrics, ~ emmeans(mB[[.x]]$pooled, ~ Fava_g * Inoc, at = list(Fava_g = grid),
                                          type = "response") %>% as.data.frame() %>% norm_cl() %>%
                    mutate(metric = .x)) %>%
  left_join(rngB, by = "Inoc") %>% filter(Fava_g >= lo, Fava_g <= hi) %>% rel()
annB <- slopeB %>% filter(metric %in% plot_metrics) %>% select(metric, Inoc, kind, p.value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = kind, values_from = p.value) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("slope ", fmt_p(pooled), " (pooled)\nslope ", fmt_p(adjusted), " (adj. for water)")) %>% rel()
inoc_panel <- c(Inoc = "Inter - inoculated", Strl = "Inter - sterile")

figB <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = linesB, aes(Fava_g, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), fill = blue, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = linesB, aes(Fava_g, response), color = blue, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = ptsA, aes(Fava_g, y, shape = Water, fill = Inoc), color = blue, size = 3, stroke = 1) +
  geom_text(data = annB, aes(x = Inf, y = 1.3, label = label), hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1,
            size = 3, color = "grey25", lineheight = 0.95) +
  facet_grid(Inoc ~ metric, scales = "free_x", labeller = labeller(Inoc = inoc_panel)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Control = 21, Moderate = 24, Severe = 22), labels = water_lab) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Inoc = blue, Strl = "white"), guide = "none") +
  guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "grey60", color = "grey30"))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.3), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Fava biomass (g per pot)", y = "Proportion of 100 root intersects",
       title = "AMF colonization against fava biomass within each inoculation treatment",
       subtitle = "Per pot, n = 15 per panel (x-axes differ by row). Line = pooled fit with 95% CI; shape = water level.") +
  theme_ms(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey93", linewidth = 0.3),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey30"))
figB
ggsave("figures/Fig_AMFvsFava_ByInoc.pdf", figB, width = 10.5, height = 7)
ggsave("figures/Fig_AMFvsFava_ByInoc.png", figB, width = 10.5, height = 7, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

# Part 3 - Total NPP against AMF metrics, Moderate and Severe drought

**Question.** Under moderate and severe drought, does wheat-pot productivity rise or fall with how
heavily the roots are colonized? Simple regression of **pot total NPP** (`Pot_NPP_g`, g per pot) on
each AMF metric, **fitted separately for every water level and every stand type** (as requested; Control is
left out). This departs from the "fit once" convention used elsewhere, so each regression has only
n = 10 pots and the 12 tests below are unadjusted.

* Stand types are kept apart, never pooled: Mono pots hold 12 wheat plants and Inter pots 6 wheat + 1
  fava, so their pot totals are not on one scale. In Inter pots the total includes the fava.
* Predictors are the proportion of 100 root intersects (0-1): any fungal structure, arbuscules, vesicles.
* Model: `lm(log(Pot_NPP_g) ~ metric)`. The slope is the log-change in NPP per unit change in the
  proportion, reported as the percent change per +0.10 colonization.
* **Colonization is nearly a proxy for inoculation.** Within each cell, sterile pots sit near 0 and
  inoculated pots near 1 for hyphae, so the hyphal slope is close to an inoculation contrast. Points
  are colored by Inoc so the two clusters are visible. Arbuscules and vesicles vary more within the
  inoculated pots, which makes them the more informative predictors.

```{r modelsC}
wheat_all <- readRDS("../wheat_audited.rds") %>% filter(Water %in% c("Moderate", "Severe")) %>%
  mutate(Water = droplevels(Water))
stopifnot(nrow(wheat_all) == 40, all(table(wheat_all$Poly, wheat_all$Inoc, wheat_all$Water) == 5),
          all(wheat_all$Pot_NPP_g > 0))

dfC <- wheat_all %>%
  select(Poly, Inoc, Water, Pot_NPP_g, all_of(plot_metrics)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(plot_metrics), names_to = "metric", values_to = "n") %>%
  mutate(x = n / 100)

fitC <- dfC %>% group_by(Poly, Water, metric) %>% nest() %>%
  mutate(m = map(data, ~ lm(log(Pot_NPP_g) ~ x, data = .x)),
         est = map_dbl(m, ~ coef(.x)[["x"]]),
         se  = map_dbl(m, ~ summary(.x)$coefficients["x", 2]),
         p   = map_dbl(m, ~ summary(.x)$coefficients["x", 4]),
         pct10 = (exp(est * 0.1) - 1) * 100,
         n = map_int(data, nrow))

fitC %>% ungroup() %>%
  transmute(Poly, Water, metric = metric_lab[metric], n, `slope (log)` = round(est, 2), SE = round(se, 2),
            `% per +0.10` = round(pct10, 1), p = signif(p, 3)) %>%
  arrange(Poly, Water, metric) %>% knitr::kable()
```

```{r figC, fig.width=10.5, fig.height=11}
gridC <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 100)
linesC <- fitC %>%
  mutate(pred = map2(m, data, function(m, d) {
    g <- tibble(x = gridC[gridC >= min(d$x) & gridC <= max(d$x)])
    pr <- predict(m, g, se.fit = TRUE)
    tcrit <- qt(0.975, m$df.residual)
    g %>% mutate(fit = exp(pr$fit), lcl = exp(pr$fit - tcrit * pr$se.fit), ucl = exp(pr$fit + tcrit * pr$se.fit))
  })) %>% select(Poly, Water, metric, pred) %>% unnest(pred)

annC <- fitC %>% ungroup() %>%
  transmute(Poly, Water, metric,
            label = paste0(fmt_p(p), " (", sprintf("%+.1f", round(pct10, 1) + 0), "% per +0.10)"))

relC <- function(d) d %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, plot_metrics, metric_lab),
         row = factor(paste(Poly, "-", Water),
                      c("Inter - Moderate", "Inter - Severe", "Mono - Moderate", "Mono - Severe")))
linesC <- relC(linesC); annC <- relC(annC); ptsC <- relC(dfC)

figC <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = linesC, aes(x, ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl, fill = Poly), alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(data = linesC, aes(x, fit, color = Poly), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = ptsC, aes(x, Pot_NPP_g, color = Poly, shape = Inoc), size = 3, stroke = 1.1) +
  geom_text(data = annC, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label), hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.4,
            size = 3, color = "grey25") +
  facet_grid(row ~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_poly, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_poly, guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shp_inoc, labels = inoc_lab,
                     guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = "grey30"))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +
  labs(x = "Proportion of 100 root intersects", y = "Pot total NPP (g per pot)",
       title = "Pot productivity against AMF colonization under moderate and severe drought",
       subtitle = "Separate simple regression per panel, n = 10.") +
  theme_ms(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey93", linewidth = 0.3),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey30"))
figC
ggsave("figures/Fig_NPPvsAMF_Drought.pdf", figC, width = 10.5, height = 11)
ggsave("figures/Fig_NPPvsAMF_Drought.png", figC, width = 10.5, height = 11, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```
